subject: Private VPC: geo-lock, retention slices, and finalizer scrub process
messages:
From: Tom Berger <tom.berger@aegishealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data locality & deletion: questions for Private/VPC deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Before we lock down the Private deployment, Aegis needs a clear, auditable answer to a few items around customer-controlled storage and deletion workflows. High level questions: 

- Can customer data be constrained to a single region (we need US-west only) with guarantees there is no cross-region replication except for explicit, customer-authorized DR?
- For retention, can we set per-tenant retention windows (e.g., medical test data = 7 years, ephemeral analytics = 30 days) and have those honored by the platform?
- When a tenant is requested to be deleted, what exactly is removed and how soon? We're specifically asking about any intermediate snapshots, backups, or cold replicas.
- What evidence can you provide when deletion is completed (manifest, checksums, signatures)? We have to present this to our compliance officer.

We're on a tight timeline — can you provide a short written flow and any templates you use so we can evaluate?

Appreciate it,
Tom

--
Tom Berger
Head of Cloud Security, AegisHealth

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berger <tom.berger@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data locality & deletion: questions for Private/VPC deployment

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: yes, the Private/VPC offering supports region-scoped (non-replicated) storage, tenant-level retention policies, and an auditable deletion finalizer. Below I outline the high-level flow and attach a short runbook. I've CC'd Dev for the technical deletion finalizer details and Marissa for compliance attestation timing.

High-level:
- Geo-locking: When we provision your Private control plane, we can limit the storage endpoints to a single cloud region (we use the region's storage endpoints and do not enable cross-region replication unless you request it). If you opt for customer-managed buckets (recommended), the customer retains full control over the bucket region.
- Retention slices: We support per-tenant retention policies. Policies can be enforced using lifecycle rules (customer-managed) or our policy engine (Redwood-managed) that tags objects with retention labels.
- Finalizer & deletion: Deletion is a multi-step process: mark tenant -> purge runtime caches/prefixes -> delete live objects -> remove snapshots/snapshotted volumes -> schedule key destruction (if using Redwood-managed keys) -> produce evidence manifest.
- Evidence: We provide a deletion manifest (object list + hashes + timestamps) and an attestation PDF signed by our compliance team.

I've attached: scrub-runbook.pdf (high-level flow). Next step — if this looks good we can schedule a technical deep-dive where Dev walks through object lifecycle behaviors and how we handle backups/replication.

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berger <tom.berger@aegishealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data locality & deletion: questions for Private/VPC deployment

Tom — diving into the mechanics you asked about. I know you care about exact deletion semantics, so below is the operational flow we follow in Private/VPC deployments (customer-managed storage vs Redwood-managed storage noted):

Flow (customer-managed buckets — recommended):
1) Request: Aegis requests tenant deletion via Console API or signed SOW. Ticket created and assigned.
2) Quiesce: We flip tenant to "pending_delete" to prevent new writes and trigger immediate KV/prefix cache eviction on all serving nodes. This removes runtime references quickly.
3) Live object purge: For customer-managed buckets, we issue object delete calls against your bucket using the credentials you provide (we do not copy objects out). If versioning is enabled, we delete all versions. If object lock is enabled, deletion follows your configured retention.
4) Snapshots & backups: We do not create third-party cold backups unless requested. If you have Redwood-managed snapshot replication enabled for DR, our deletion workflow will delete snapshots and their metadata during the same run; devs must mark DR snapshots for deletion. We also scan for any DB backups stored in our control plane and flag them for removal.
5) Key handling: If you use Redwood-managed KMS, we schedule key rotation -> destruction per the agreed timeline (KMS destruction is irreversible; we include key IDs in the manifest). If you use Customer-managed keys (CMK), you control the key lifecycle and can revoke/delete keys as part of your workflow.
6) Finalizer & manifest: After object deletions complete, an async finalizer compiles a deletion manifest (object paths, versions, SHA-256 hashes, deletion timestamps) and writes it to your selected evidence location (customer bucket or an encrypted Redwood evidence folder if you requested).
7) Attestation: Compliance prepares an attestation PDF with signatures and audit-trail pointers (IDs and timestamps).

Timing expectations (typical):
- Cache eviction: seconds to minutes depending on serving load.
- Live object deletion (tenant size dependent): minutes for small tenants, hours for multi-TB tenants — can be parallelized.
- Snapshot/backup removal: depends on snapshot volume; typically completes in same run but add a buffer (24–72 hrs) for large archival stores.
- Evidence pack delivered: within 10 business days by default (can be accelerated under SLA).

Deliverables we provide: deletion-manifest-template.csv (attached) and scrub-runbook.pdf (attached).

Notes/edge cases:
- If customer-managed replication exists outside the primary region, Redwood cannot delete copies in external systems; customers must coordinate revocation in those systems.
- For on-prem or air-gapped Private installs, disk sanitization is performed by site ops; we provide a signed wipe certificate upon completion.

Let me know if you want the CLI/API call examples and IAM role requirements — I can include them in the deep-dive.

—Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Berger <tom.berger@aegishealth.com>

Subject: Re: Data locality & deletion: questions for Private/VPC deployment

Thanks Irene/Dev — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team: 

- Backups/replicas: we want explicit confirmation that Redwood will not, by default, create cold backups in another region without written approval. Your note implies that but please confirm in writing.
- Evidence SLA: 10 business days is acceptable for routine deletes, but for regulated patient record erasures we need faster delivery for the attestation. What are options to accelerate to 3 business days (paid SLA)?

If you can confirm the non-replication default policy in writing and give a short note on paid acceleration, we can move to an SOW addendum.

Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Berger <tom.berger@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data locality & deletion: questions for Private/VPC deployment

Tom — quick compliance confirmation and options.

1) Replication policy: Confirmed — Redwood Private will not enable cross-region cold backups or replication by default. Any cross-region replication, cold backup retention, or additional DR copies must be explicitly documented in the SOW and signed by both parties. We will include this clause in the SOW addendum.

2) Evidence SLA acceleration: We offer a Paid Evidence Fast-Track add-on. Options: 
   - Standard: Evidence pack within 10 business days (no additional fee).
   - Fast-Track: Evidence pack within 3 business days (fee: one-time $6,500 per deletion event or negotiable for volume).
   - Notarized Witness Delete: We can provide a notarized attestation with optional third-party witness (time varies, additional cost applies).

Attached: attestation-sample.pdf (template) and I will work with Irene to add the non-replication clause to your SOW. If acceptable, we can spin an SOW addendum and a Fast-Track add-on quote for procurement.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Compliance & Trust, Redwood Inference
